subject: Pilot extension: LOI vs credit-based option for Orion Health
messages:
From: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@orionhealth.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Quick ask — extra 3 weeks on pilot + pricing clarity

Hi Mateo,

We hit a small scheduling snag on the integration side and are behind on validation by about two weeks. The team is asking whether we can extend the current 30-day pilot by an additional three weeks so we can finish the last set of throughput tests.

A couple of asks:
- Could you confirm whether an extension would be provided as additional calendar days or as credit we can apply against extra tokens/embeddings?
- If we agree to a short LOI (letter of intent) committing to a follow-on pilot/POC at a small committed spend, do you have a short-term discount you can offer?

We need something quick to share with procurement/legal. Happy to hop on a 20-min call if easier.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Jenkins
Head of Platform Integrations
Orion Health

Subject: Re: Quick ask — extra 3 weeks on pilot + pricing clarity

Sara — thanks for the note and sorry to hear about the scheduling slide. Short answers up front: we can do either additional days or a credit, and we can put a short LOI in place for a modest discount if you can commit to a minimal follow-on engagement.

Two options I recommend (details attached):
1) Time-extension: Add 21 calendar days to the existing pilot window. No change to current billing — we just keep the environment active and keep current limits.
2) Credit top-up: Issue a token/embedding credit bucket equivalent to expected additional usage (we modeled 150k tokens / 10k embeddings) that Orion can redeem during the extension window. Credits expire 30 days after issuance.

For the LOI path, we can offer a 12% discount off our standard pilot hourly/throughput surcharge if Orion signs a one-page LOI (term: 90 days to commit to a paid POC with a minimum $45k committed spend). I attached: LOI_Draft_v1.pdf and a pricing_table_options.xlsx with line items and the discount math.

Next steps suggestion: I can open an LOI draft and loop in Kimberly for any SLA/termination carveouts, and Rishi for finance approval on the discount. If that looks OK to you, I’ll send the DocuSign link and aim for signature by EOD Monday to keep timelines tight.

—Mateo

Thanks, Mateo — looping in a couple of legal/ops checks. A few items we need in the LOI before we push to DocuSign:
- Data handling confirmation for the extended window (retention, deletion timeline)
- Minimal SLA language for the reserved environment (uptime objective during extension)
- Clear acceptance criteria for the pilot extension (so both teams have the same end-state)

Sara — our usual approach is to keep the LOI high level and move the SLA specifics to the project intake / implementation appendix. If Orion needs explicit SLA language in the LOI, we can add a 48-hour availability objective and a rollback clause for any sustained performance degradation.

I’ll propose slightly revised language and send as an updated LOI so procurement/legal have something to review.

-Kimberly

Adding the finance view — the 12% discount on the LOI path is OK if we get the $45k minimum committed spend within the 90-day conversion window and we tie the discount explicitly to the LOI (no retrospective price changes). A few quick clarifications:
- Can the committed spend be a mix of reserved tokens + implementation workshops? (Answer: yes, up to 30% of committed spend may be used toward professional services)
- Please confirm who owns the unused credits if Orion converts early or decides not to proceed after the conversion window (standard: credits are non-refundable; we can allow a 30-day grace for transfer to a follow-on agreement).

If those points are acceptable, I’ll greenlight the DocuSign link from our side.

-Rishi
